claims.text: A model that separately predicts lattice and electronic thermal conductivity will predict the total thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr more accurately than Debye-temperature-based approaches.
DFT-derived anharmonic phonon spectra can account for lattice thermal conductivity, including impurity and defect scattering.
An electron Boltzmann transport formulation incorporating electron–phonon interactions can predict the electronic thermal conductivity.
The lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions in HfNbTaTiZr are comparable below 200 K.
HfNbTaTiZr containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen has a total thermal conductivity of 10–17 W/(K·m) over 300–1200 K.
The proposed model will reduce prediction error by at least approximately 30% relative to traditional analytical models.
The proposed model will predict total thermal conductivity within ±20% of experiment throughout 100–1200 K.
Intrinsic atomic-scale disorder and local bonding variations in HfNbTaTiZr produce distinct phonon- and electron-scattering mechanisms.
Simplified average models do not adequately capture the distinct scattering mechanisms in HfNbTaTiZr.

Accounting for anharmonicity, phonon lifetimes, impurity scattering, defect scattering, and electron–phonon interactions separately provides a more realistic transport description than approaches based on averaged parameters.
Conventional methods use average Debye temperatures, effective masses, and force-constant estimates without distinguishing lattice and electronic heat transport.
The model is intended to apply to well-characterized, single-phase HfNbTaTiZr with controlled impurity and oxygen levels.
The model may not apply to samples with significant defect concentrations or phase segregation because additional scattering mechanisms may dominate.
Uncertainty remains in the low-temperature scattering parameters.
Subtle microstructural features may affect transport but may not be represented in perfectly ordered DFT models.
The hypothesis is refuted if predicted lattice or electronic contributions differ from measured values by more than ±20%.
The hypothesis is refuted if the model fails to achieve a 30% error reduction relative to conventional Debye-based models.

contradictions.description: The intervention and mechanism say that defect and impurity scattering are explicitly included, whereas the uncertainty field describes the DFT models as perfectly ordered and unable to capture subtle microstructural features. It is therefore unclear whether defect and impurity structures are actually represented or only treated through an auxiliary approximation.

The initial state combines 'high-purity, near defect-free' specimens with approximately 1 wt.% oxygen, but the hypothesis does not clarify whether that oxygen level is considered compatible with the stated near-defect-free condition or how its associated defects are controlled.
